questions.q: Beauty was a "job horse." What does that mean in this chapter?
choices: A horse hired out to all sorts of people
A horse that only pulls carts full of bricks
A horse kept for racing at the country fairs
A horse that works the fields on a farm
questions.evidence: I was a "job horse", and was let out to all sorts of people who wished to hire me

questions.q: Why was Beauty often let out to ignorant drivers?
choices: He was gentle and could be depended upon
He was the cheapest horse in the whole stable
He was the fastest horse the master owned
No other horse there was strong enough for it
questions.evidence: as I was good-tempered and gentle

questions.q: What do tight-rein drivers do wrong?
choices: Never relax the hard pull on the horse's mouth
Let the reins lie loose on the horse's back
Refuse to ever use the whip, even on hills
Drive far too slowly, even on flat roads
questions.evidence: never relaxing the pull on the horse's mouth

questions.q: What is the problem with loose-rein drivers?
choices: They have no control if something happens suddenly
They pull too hard on the bit the whole time
They jerk the reins so the bit cuts the horse's mouth
They will only drive out late at night
questions.evidence: such gentlemen have no control over a horse, if anything happens suddenly

questions.q: What did Squire Gordon say spoiling a horse was just as cruel as?
choices: Spoiling a child
Whipping a dog
Starving a cat
Selling a friend
questions.evidence: just as cruel as spoiling a child

questions.q: Why did Beauty get a stone in his foot on the phaeton trip?
choices: The driver was laughing and talking, not watching
Beauty ran off the road on purpose to rest
A passing cart's wheel flicked it up into his hoof
The lady asked to drive and steered onto the verge
questions.evidence: he never thought it worth while to keep an eye on his horse

questions.q: How did the careless driver react when he finally saw Beauty was lame?
choices: He blamed the stable for sending a lame horse
He got down at once and checked Beauty's feet
He said sorry to Beauty and stroked his neck
He turned around and drove straight back home
questions.evidence: Why, they have sent us out with a lame horse! What a shame!

questions.q: Who took the stone out of Beauty's foot?
choices: A farmer riding a brown cob
The lady sitting in the phaeton
The careless young driver
A policeman on the corner
questions.evidence: a farmer came riding up on a brown cob

questions.q: What did the farmer use to get the wedged stone out?
choices: A stone-pick from his pocket
His bare fingers and thumb
The handle of the driver's whip
A knife borrowed from the lady
questions.evidence: he drew a stone-pick out of his pocket

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: How bad and ignorant drivers hurt job horses
How Beauty won a race against a farmer's cob
How a phaeton is built and kept in repair
How Beauty learned to pull heavy brick carts
questions.evidence: all the different kinds of bad and ignorant driving to which we horses are subjected
